prompt.context: This is a quick brainteaser case.
prompt.question: Please estimate the number of passenger car tires sold each year in the United States.

clarifying_info.q: How many new cars are sold each year?
clarifying_info.a: About 10 million new cars are sold each year.

clarifying_info.q: How long do cars last before replacement?
clarifying_info.a: Cars last about 7 years before needing replacement.

clarifying_info.q: How many miles do people drive per year?
Should I assume people purchase new tires when needed?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, assume people purchase new tires when needed.

clarifying_info.q: Should I assume growth in the number of cars on the road?
clarifying_info.a: Assume no growth in installed cars.

clarifying_info.q: How many tires does a new car come with?
clarifying_info.a: Bonus consideration: new cars get 5 tires (including spare); old cars needing replacement get 4 new tires.

framework: Segment the market into two buckets: (1) tires on new cars sold and (2) replacement tires for the existing installed base.
Estimate the total installed car base from the new-car sales and average car lifespan.
Estimate how often the installed base needs new tires using miles driven per year and tire lifespan.
Sum both segments to get total annual tire sales; optionally adjust for spare tires.

questions.prompt: How many cars are currently on the road in the United States?
questions.guidance: Use the fact that 10M new cars are sold per year and cars last ~7 years. Steady-state installed base = 10M x 7 = 70M cars. Of these, 10M are new and 60M are older (already on the road).

math.setup: Installed base = annual new car sales x average car life
math.answer: 70M total cars on the road (10M new, 60M old)

questions.prompt: How often does the average car need new tires?
questions.guidance: Divide tire lifespan in miles by annual miles driven to get years per tire set. This gives the replacement cycle.

math.setup: Tire lifespan (miles) / Annual miles driven = years per tire replacement

questions.prompt: How many replacement tires are sold each year for the existing installed base?
questions.guidance: Divide the number of old cars by the replacement cycle to find how many cars need new tires each year, then multiply by 4 tires per car.

math.setup: (Old installed cars / replacement cycle) x tires per car
steps: Cars needing new tires per year = 60M / 3 = 20M

questions.prompt: How many tires are sold with new cars each year?
questions.guidance: Multiply annual new car sales by tires per new car. Base case is 4; bonus case is 5 including the spare.

math.setup: New car sales x tires per new car

questions.prompt: What is the total number of passenger car tires sold each year in the United States?
questions.guidance: Add replacement tires and new-car tires. Present both the no-spare and with-spare answer.

recommendation: Approximately 120–130 million passenger car tires are sold in the United States each year.
The range reflects whether new cars are counted with 4 tires (120M) or 5 tires including the spare (130M).
risks: Actual tire lifespan varies by driving behavior, tire quality, and climate.
The assumption of a static installed car base ignores long-run growth or contraction in vehicle ownership.
Commercial vehicles, SUVs, and trucks are excluded; including them would raise the total significantly.
next_steps: Validate the 70M installed base against government vehicle registration data.
Refine the replacement cycle using industry data on average tire mileage and consumer behavior.
Segment further by tire type (all-season, performance, truck) to size sub-markets if needed.
